title: Draw a letter from its bits
description:
A bitmap font stores each row of a letter as a number: its bits say which pixels are on. Read **7 numbers**, one per line: the rows of a 5-pixel-wide letter, top to bottom. Print the letter: `#` for a 1 bit, `.` for a 0, with the bit worth 16 on the left and the bit worth 1 on the right.

The input `17 17 17 31 17 17 17` (one per line) is the H from the lesson:

```
#...#
#...#
#...#
#####
#...#
#...#
#...#
```

To test bit *k* of a number `n`: `(n >> k) & 1` is 1 when the bit is on. `range(4, -1, -1)` counts 4, 3, 2, 1, 0.
hints: For each row, go through the bit values 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 (bits 4 down to 0) and add `#` or `.` to a string, then print the string.
lessonTitle: How Text Gets on the Screen
